To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bryophyte communities were more diverse in mixed deciduous forest than in even-aged stands, and the diversity was higher in stands with more tree species and structural heterogeneity, and with a higher amount of dead wood.
ground-floor bryophytes are positively influenced by tree species and structural diversity, and by substrate availability (open soil and logs) and negatively by the litter of decidu-ous trees.

the species richness of forest floor brynophytes is positively related to the diversity of tree species, stand structural characteristics and dead wood volume in the studied region, while the cover of the bryophyte communities is positively related to light heterogeneity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of forest management on the bryophytes of temperate forests and provides a basis for further research on the effects of forest structure on the bryophyte communities of Central Europe.
the importance of stand structure and tree species composition in the conservation of forest-floor bryophytes in temperate mixed deciduous forests.
the effects of forest structure on the diversity of bryophyta in a mixed deciduous forest of Western Hungary.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ground-floor bryophytes of temperate mixed forests are affected by the tree species composition, the structure and the substrate availability of stands.
the effects of tree species composition and stand structure on the ground-floor bryophytes are not independent but interactive.
the ground-floor bryoflora is more sensitive to the effects of stand structure than to tree species composition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bryophyte specialists can be maintained in the studied forests only in stands with high dead-wood volume and high tree species diversity.
bryophyte communities can be maintained in managed forests by preserving the natural tree species composition and structural diversity of the forest floor.
the forest management should aim at maintaining a heterogeneous forest floor, with sufficient amount of dead wood, open soil, and a diverse stand structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ground-floor bryoflora of mixed deciduous forest is more sensitive to changes in tree species composition and stand structural characteristics than to changes in light availability, and therefore the effects of forest management should be considered carefully.
stand structural characteristics and substrate availability are important factors in shaping ground-floor bryoflora in temperate mixed forest.
the effects of forest structure on bryophytic communities can be detected at a large scale and the results can be applied in the management of temperate forests in Western Hungary.
